title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This is the end of a discussion begun on p.35, set in the axiomatics of a class W of 'weak equivalences' in (Cat) or in a presheaf topos Â, with W_A the induced class. A category is W-aspherical if its map to the point is in W, i.e. it is 'contractible relative to W'. On the previous page Grothendieck notes three things. First, a condition he calls (ii) is stable under sums, but another condition is not, so the implication (i) ⇒ (ii) is strict. Second, a groupoid example shows that (ii) plus connectedness does not force W-asphericity. Third, compatibility with finite products works directly in (Cat), because a finite product of maps in W is in W. For infinite products he would need to know that a product of maps in W is in W, in (Cat) or in some Â, the latter implying the former. He remarks that even for the usual weak equivalence W_0 this is not evident to him. This page closes the thought. He thinks there is a good chance of getting there. He then poses the key question: is a product ∏_{i∈I} X_i of W-aspherical objects (or 'spaces') again W-aspherical? He judges this at least as important as the question of infinite sums (coproducts). The underlying problem is whether 'basic localizers' / asphericity notions are stable under infinite products. This would be needed for exactness properties of the localized category (Cat)[W^{-1}] (or Â[W_A^{-1}]) with respect to infinite products.
errors: The hoped-for positive answer is false for the usual weak equivalences W_0 in (Cat) and in simplicial sets (and in general in a presheaf topos). Counterexample: let Z_n be the zigzag poset 0 < 1 > 2 < 3 ... with n steps; its nerve is contractible. The nerve commutes with products, being a right adjoint. In ∏_n N(Z_n), an edge path of length k moves each coordinate by at most k steps. So the vertices (0)_n and (n)_n, the two ends of each zigzag, lie in different components. Hence ∏ Z_n is not even connected, although every factor is W_0-aspherical. The statement is true only after replacing the factors by fibrant models (Kan complexes, CW/topological spaces), i.e. for 'spaces' but not for categories or presheaves. The page leaves the question open, so this is a gap rather than an asserted error.

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether infinite products of W-aspherical objects are W-aspherical. For the usual W in Cat the answer is negative (products of zigzag posets), which a short remark settles. This explains why product stability does not appear in the later axiomatics of basic localizers.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a brief open question, and its answer for the standard localizer is a well-known folklore negative. Nothing new or unrecognized is on the page.
